title: Employment Situation (May 2027 data), 08:30 ET — the last payroll before the June FOMC, and it lands inside the blackout
source: EST: derived from BLS's own published scheduling rule as re-implemented and re-validated from scratch by the never-assessed initial research of jobs-2027-05-07 on this calendar, 2026-09-09 — the Employment Situation is released on the third Friday following the end of the reference week (the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th), a rule that scored 7 for 7 there against the four confirmed jobs-* entries (2026-09-04, 2026-10-02, 2026-11-06, 2026-12-04) and three historical Sunday-July-4 releases (2004-07-02, 2010-07-02, 2021-07-02). For May 2027 data the reference week is Sun 2027-05-09 to Sat 2027-05-15, and the third Friday after 05-15 is 2027-06-04 — an ordinary NYSE session with no holiday within a week of it, so the rule's one documented failure mode (a derived Friday landing on a closed session) cannot fire. The prefix is EST: and not BLS: because bls.gov returns 403 to this lane's plain fetchers on all three schedule routes tried 2026-09-09, fred.stlouisfed.org's release-date register returned 404, and a web search the same day found no published 2027 BLS schedule at all — the standing blind spot recorded in docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of jobs-2027-05-07, 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED at D+28 from jobs-2027-05-07 — outside the 5-day corridor and proposed anyway, because it is the fact that makes that ledger's FOMC-position leg checkable rather than asserted. It is the LAST payroll before fomc-2027-06-09 (est) and it lands INSIDE the blackout that opens at fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29 (est), so no Fed speaker can react to it on the record before the decision — the mirror image of jobs-2027-05-07, which is the FIRST payroll after fomc-2027-04-28 (est) with a full month of Fed commentary ahead of it. It also fills a real gap in this calendar's 2027 coverage: the tracked jobs-* set currently jumps from 2027-05-07 straight to 2027-07-02. Unlike the May 2027 refunding auction dates — which the same session measured as NOT reliably derivable (a settlement-anchored rule scores only 88/122, the modal Tue/Wed/Thu weekday pattern only 82-98 of 120) and therefore deliberately did NOT propose — the payroll rule reproduces 7 for 7, which is why this one is filed and those are recorded as a hole instead. Impact high matches every other jobs-* entry on this calendar. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
